title: Introducing Euler's Formula on the Complex Plane
full_prompt: Write a ManimGL script using the InteractiveScene class to introduce Euler's formula. First, set up a ComplexPlane on the left side of the screen with a blue grid and coordinate labels for 1, -1, i, and -i. Draw a red arc of radius 1 representing an angle of pi, with a DecimalNumber tracking the angle as it sweeps from 0 to pi. Once the arc is complete, replace the decimal number with a red pi label. Next, write the formula 'e^{pi i} = -1' on the upper right, using LaggedStart to transform the pi label, the i label, and the -1 coordinate label from the plane into their respective positions in the formula. After a brief pause, transform the characters of the formula into the word 'Cliché?' while introducing a Randolph PiCreature on the right who says 'This again?' in a sassy tone. Finally, display a grid of YouTube thumbnails on the left representing various popular videos about Euler's formula.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing PiCreature assets or Randolph class definition
common_failure_modes.note: Randolph is a custom 3b1b class. If running in standard Manim, it must be mocked or replaced with a standard Mobject.
Loading YouTube thumbnails directly from URLs can fail if there is no internet access during rendering.
Manim Community uses Create instead of ShowCreation, and ReplacementTransform instead of FadeTransform.
